verses.zh: （大卫在献殿的时候，作这诗歌。）耶和华啊，我要尊崇你，因为你曾提拔我，不叫仇敌向我夸耀。
verses.en: A psalm, a song used at the dedication of the temple;[NOTE:1] by David.I will praise you, O Lord, for you lifted me up[NOTE:2] and did not allow my enemies to gloat[NOTE:3] over me.
notes: Psalm 30. The author thanks the Lord for delivering him from death and urges others to join him in praise. The psalmist experienced divine discipline for a brief time, but when he cried out for help the Lord intervened and restored his favor.

Heb “a song of the dedication of the house.” The referent of “house” is unclear. It is possible that David wrote this psalm for the dedication ceremony of Solomon’s temple. Another possibility is that the psalm was used on the occasion of the dedication of the second temple following the return from exile, or on the occasion of the rededication of the temple in Maccabean times.

Elsewhere the verb דָּלָה (dalah) is used of drawing water from a well (Exod 2:16, 19; Prov 20:5). The psalmist was trapped in the pit leading to Sheol (see v. 3), but the Lord hoisted him up. The Piel stem is used here, perhaps suggesting special exertion on the Lord’s part.
verses.commentary:
30:1-5 The psalmist extols and praises YHWH
for deliverance from death, either by attack or by illness.

30:1 "I will extol" This VERB (BDB 926, KB 1202,
Polel IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE
sense) has two primary meanings.

- to exalt, extol (here of YHWH), cf. Exod. 15:2; Ps. 34:3; 99:5,9;
107:32; 118:28; 145:1; Isa. 25:1

- to lift up (referring to praise of YHWH), cf. 2 Sam. 22:47; Ps. 18:46;
21:13; 46:10; 57:5,11

This praise is given because YHWH has acted.

- He lifted up (BDB 194, KB 222, Piel PERFECT)
the psalmist, Ps. 30:1 (this term was used of drawing water from a well
and may refer to divine rescue from the pit, cf. Ps. 30:4).

- He did not let the psalmist's enemies rejoice (BDB 33, KB 38, Qal
PARTICIPLE), cf. Ps. 25:2; 41:11.

- He healed him (BDB 750, KB 1272, Qal IMPERFECT
with waw), Ps. 30:2.

- He brought his soul up from Sheol (BDB 748, KB 828, Hiphil
PERFECT), Ps. 30:3.

- He has kept him alive (BDB 310, KB 309, Piel PERFECT), Ps. 30:3.

verses.zh: 耶和华―我的　神啊，我曾呼求你，你医治了我。
verses.en: O Lord my God,I cried out to you and you healed me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “rejoice.”
verses.commentary:
30:2 "O Lord my God" This is two
of the most common designations of Israel's Deity (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.).

- YHWH – God as Savior, the covenant-making God, cf. Gen. 2:3

- Elohim – God as creator and provider of all life on this planet, cf. Gen. 1:1

Notice how this Psalm starts with this title (Ps. 30:2) and ends with this
title (Ps. 30:12). This is typical of Hebraic literary style (i.e., inclusio).

▣ "You healed me" See
SPECIAL
TOPIC: HEALING

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你曾把我的灵魂从阴间救上来，使我存活，不至于下坑。
verses.en: O Lord, you pulled me[NOTE:1] up from Sheol;you rescued me from among those descending into the grave.[NOTE:2]
notes: You healed me. Apparently the psalmist was plagued by a serious illness that threatened his life. See Ps 41.
Or “my life.”
verses.commentary:
30:3 "Sheol. . .pit" These two
terms (synonymous parallelism) refer to the grave or the holding place of
the dead. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?, I. B.

Notice that antithetical parallelism common in this Psalm. It demonstrates the "two ways"
of Deut. 30:15,19; Psalm 1.

For a good brief discussion of "pit" see IVP, Dictionary of
Biblical Imagery, p. 646-647.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEBREW POETRY, III. A. #2

verses.zh: 耶和华的圣民哪，你们要歌颂他，称赞他可记念的圣名。
verses.en: Sing to the Lord, you faithful followers[NOTE:1] of his;give thanks to his holy name.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “you kept me alive from those descending into the pit.” The Hebrew noun בּוֹר (bor, “pit, cistern”) is sometimes used of the grave and/or the realm of the dead. The translation follows the consonantal Hebrew text (Kethib); the marginal reading (Qere) has, “you kept me alive so that I did not go down into the pit.”
A “faithful follower” (חָסִיד) is one who does what is right in God’s eyes and remains faithful to God (see Pss 4:3; 12:1; 16:10; 31:23; 37:28; 86:2; 97:10).
verses.commentary:
30:4

NASB
"godly ones"

NKJV, Peshitta
"saints"

NRSV
"faithful ones"

TEV
"faithful people"

JPSOA
"you faithful"

NJB
"who are faithful"

LXX
"you devout"

This ADJECTIVE (BDB 339, KB 336 II) is formed from the
NOUN hesed (BDB 338), which denoted
covenant loyalty.

- On God's part; He is faithful to His covenant promises.

- On the faithful follower's part; he/she must be obedient and steadfast to their covenant obligations.

It becomes a common title in the Psalms for faithful covenant followers
(i.e., Ps. 4:3 and many more). Several translations (TEV, NJB) see Ps. 30:4-5
as a separate strophe imploring faithful followers to join in the praise
of YHWH (see paragraph divisions on the front page of this Psalm).

In this context they are called to

- sing praise – BDB 274 I, KB 273, Piel IMPERATIVE

- give thanks – BDB 392, KB 389, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (HESED)

▣

NASB, NRSV, JPSOA
"name"

NKJV, Peshitta
"remembrance"

TEV
"remember"

NJB
"unforgettable"

The MT has the NOUN "remembrance" or
"memorial" (BDB 271, cf. Hos. 12:5). Here it refers to YHWH's
gracious character and powerful acts on behalf of His people (cf. Ps. 6:5;
30:5; 97:12; 102:12; 111:4; 145:7).

The Hebrew concept of "name"
is here, but not the word. Both occur in parallel in Ps. 135:13 and Isa.
26:8. Also notice the focus on "memorial-name" in Exod. 3:15.

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

verses.zh: 因为，他的怒气不过是转眼之间；他的恩典乃是一生之久。一宿虽然有哭泣，早晨便必欢呼。
verses.en: For his anger lasts only a brief moment,and his good favor restores one’s life.[NOTE:1] One may experience sorrow during the night,but joy arrives in the morning.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “to his holy remembrance.” The noun זֵכֵר (zekher, “remembrance”) here refers to the name of the Lord as invoked in liturgy and praise. Cf. Pss 6:5; 97:12. The Lord’s “name” is “holy” in the sense that it is a reminder of his uniqueness and greatness.

Heb “for [there is] a moment in his anger, [but] life in his favor.” Because of the parallelism with “moment,” some understand חַיִּים (khayyim) in a quantitative sense: “lifetime” (cf. NIV, NRSV). However, the immediate context, which emphasizes deliverance from death (see v. 3), suggests that חַיִּים has a qualitative sense: “physical life” or even “prosperous life” (cf. NEB “in his favour there is life”).
verses.commentary:
30:5 This verse has captured the wonder of
grace to fallen humanity (antithetical parallel). This is a fallen world
but YHWH would not allow the broken fellowship of Eden to be permanent.
There are consequences to sin and rebellion but by His grace, mediated
through a faithful follower's faith (cf. Eph. 2:8-9), there is forgiveness
and restoration (cf. Ps. 103:8-14; Isa. 54:7-8)! The only permanent
consequence is unbelief. It is the unpardonable sin.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE UNPARDONABLE SIN and

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIN UNTO DEATH

The first two lines of Ps. 30:5 have no VERBS. The TENSE
structure emphasizes the theological personification of life's experiences as a traveler.

"For a moment His anger

For a lifetime His favour!"

The AB (p. 182) suggests that "lifetime" (BDB 213) means "eternal
life," based on Ps. 21:4. However, Ps. 91:16 is the normal OT usage
of this word, which refers to this life.

Just an added thought about "anger" in this context. The OT saw
a linkage between sin and sickness (cf. James 5:13-18). Jesus seems to
modify this view in John 9:1-12. If God judged us in light of our sin we
would all be sick and dying. The wonderful truth is we deserve "anger"
but we get mercy, grace, and love! We, however, are not all healed (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: IS HEALING GOD'S PLAN FOR EVERY AGE?)! Yet,
He is with us in our sufferings (cf. Rom. 8:18-25; 2 Cor. 4:17).

▣ "His anger" This root (BDB
60) is related to "nose" (i.e., red face) or "snort"
(unspoken but vocal sign of human emotion).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (ANTHROPOMORPHISM)

verses.zh: 至于我，我凡事平顺便说：我永不动摇。
verses.en: In my self-confidence I said,“I will never be shaken.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “in the evening weeping comes to lodge, but at morning a shout of joy.” “Weeping” is personified here as a traveler who lodges with one temporarily.
verses.commentary:
30:6-9 This strophe seems to reflect the
fulfillment of the covenant promises of Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28.
YHWH wanted to prosper His people to show the world His character. The
psalmist, as a faithful follower, is asserting what YHWH did for him.

- prospered him

- gave him stability (i.e., "I will never be moved")

- made him strong (i.e., figure of a mountain; LXX has "my majesty")

- answered his prayers

- protected him from death so he could praise YHWH's faithfulness (BDB 54)

The AB (p. 182) sees this strophe as a warning against the sin of
overconfidence. The UBS Handbook (p. 282) sees it as his past
inappropriate experience. However, I prefer the Leviticus 26 and
Deuteronomy 28 confidence. The Handbook asserts that this Psalm,
like Psalm 29, is a chiastic pattern. If this is true then the middle of
the chiasm should be the main truth. But note the middle would be Ps. 30:6,
which both the UBS Handbook and AB say is an inappropriate
experience. You cannot have it both ways!

30:7b It is unsure how Ps. 30:7b fits with Ps. 30:7a,c. The two VERBS
(PERFECTS) describe a settled condition.

- You hid Your face – BDB 711, KB 771, Hiphil PERFECT,
"face," refers to personal presence, he felt YHWH had left him, was not available,
did not hear his prayers.

- I was (BDB 224, KB 243, Qal PERFECT)
dismayed – BDB 96, KB 111, Niphal PARTICIPLE.
This term means "disturbed," "dismayed," or "terrified,"
cf. Job 4:5; 23:15; Ps. 6:2-3; 83:17; 90:7; 104:29; Isa. 13:8; 21:3; Jer.
51:32; Ezek. 26:18.

The JPSOA sees Ps. 30:7b in contrast to Ps. 30:8, YHWH made the psalmist
"firm as a mighty mountain," but if/when He hid His face, it
brought "terror." Therefore, he called out to YHWH in prayer (Ps.
30:8). Prosperity alone, even covenant prosperity (cf. Leviticus 26;
Deuteronomy 28) is not enough! We need God! We need to feel His presence
and pleasure! We were created (cf. Gen. 1:26-27; 3:8) for fellowship with
God. Nothing, nothing else can meet this need!

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你曾施恩，叫我的江山稳固；你掩了面，我就惊惶。
verses.en: O Lord, in your good favor you made me secure.[NOTE:1] Then you rejected me[NOTE:2] and I was terrified.
notes: In my self-confidence I said… Here the psalmist begins to fill in the background of the crisis referred to in the earlier verses. He had been arrogant and self-confident, so the Lord withdrew his protection and allowed trouble to invade his life (vv. 8-11).

Heb “in your good favor you caused to stand for my mountain strength.” Apparently this means “you established strength for my mountain” (“mountain” in this case representing his rule, which would be centered on Mt. Zion) or “you established strength as my mountain” (“mountain” in this case being a metaphor for security).

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，我曾求告你；我向耶和华恳求，说：
verses.en: To you, O Lord, I cried out;I begged the Lord for mercy:[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “you hid your face.” The idiom “hide the face” can mean “ignore” (see Pss 10:11; 13:1; 51:9) or, as here, carry the stronger idea of “reject” (see Ps 88:14).

verses.zh: 我被害流血，下到坑中，有甚么益处呢？尘土岂能称赞你，传说你的诚实么？
verses.en: “What[NOTE:1] profit is there in taking my life,[NOTE:2] in my descending into the Pit?[NOTE:3] Can the dust of the grave[NOTE:4] praise you?Can it declare your loyalty?[NOTE:5]
notes: The prefixed verbal forms in v. 8 are probably preterites; the psalmist recalls that he prayed in his time of crisis.
The following two verses (vv. 9-10) contain the prayer (or an excerpt of the prayer) that the psalmist offered to the Lord during his crisis.
Heb “What profit [is there] in my blood?” “Blood” here represents his life.
The Hebrew term שָׁחַת (shakhat, “pit”) is often used as a title for Sheol (see Pss 16:10; 49:9; 55:24 HT [55:23 ET]; 103:4).
Heb “dust.” The words “of the grave” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
verses.commentary:
30:9
There are two rhetorical questions
which, in context, expect a "no" reply.

▣ "in my blood" This is an idiom for death. See

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLOOD

▣ "dust" This (BDB 779) is a
figurative expression for death (cf. Psalm 22:15,29; Isaiah 26:19; 29:4)
or Sheol/pit. Humans were made of clay/dust (cf. Gen. 2:7) and to
dust we return at death (cf. Gen. 3:19).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD? I. B.

▣ "will dust praise You?" In
the OT death was a conscious, but silent, existence (cf. Ps. 6:5;
88:11-12; Eccl. 9:10; Isa. 38:18-19).

▣ "Your faithfulness" This is an OT concept of divine loyalty
to His covenant promises to Israel (BDB 54).

YHWH is faithful (BDB 54) and loyal (BDB 338) to His covenant. He is the
One who does not change (cf. Mal. 3:6; Ps. 102:27; James 1:17; also note
Heb. 13:8). Our hope, as faithful followers, is in the unchanging,
merciful character of YHWH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Believe, Trust, Faith, and
Faithfulness in the Old Testament (אמן)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你应允我，怜恤我！耶和华啊，求你帮助我！
verses.en: Hear, O Lord, and have mercy on me.O Lord, deliver me.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The rhetorical questions anticipate the answer, “Of course not!”sn According to the OT, those who descend into the realm of death/Sheol are cut off from God’s mighty deeds and from the worshiping covenant community that experiences divine intervention (Pss 6:5; 88:10-12; Isa 38:18). In his effort to elicit a positive divine response, the psalmist reminds God that he will receive no praise or glory if he allows the psalmist to die. Dead men do not praise God!
verses.commentary:
30:10-12 This strophe starts out with three
prayer requests (IMPERATIVES).

- hear – BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE

- be gracious – BDB 335, KB 334, Qal IMPERATIVE

- be my helper (BDB 740, KB 810) – BDB 224, KB 243, Qal IMPERATIVE

Notice what YHWH's response caused in the psalmist.

- turned him from mourning into dancing

- loosed his sackcloth and girded him with gladness ("gladness" is a
poetic way of contrasting sackcloth, i.e., festival garments)

- caused him to sing praises and he will not be silent

- caused him to give thanks forever (
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER [OT])

verses.zh: 你已将我的哀哭变为跳舞，将我的麻衣脱去，给我披上喜乐，
verses.en: Then you turned my lament into dancing;you removed my sackcloth and covered me with joy.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “be a helper to me.”
verses.commentary:
30:11 "sackcloth" This was worn as a sign of mourning.

SPECIAL
TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

verses.zh: 好叫我的灵（原文是荣耀）歌颂你，并不住声。耶和华―我的　神啊，我要称谢你，直到永远！
verses.en: So now[NOTE:1] my heart[NOTE:2] will sing to you and not be silent;O Lord my God, I will always[NOTE:3] give thanks to you.
notes: Covered me with joy. “Joy” probably stands metonymically for festive attire here.
Heb “so that”; or “in order that.”

Heb “glory.” Some view כָבוֹד (khavod, “glory”) here as a metonymy for man’s inner being (see BDB 459 s.v. II כָּבוֹד 5), but it is preferable to emend the form to כְּבֵדִי (kevedi, “my liver”). Like the heart, the liver is viewed as the seat of one’s emotions. See also Pss 16:9; 57:9; 108:1, as well as H. W. Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament, 64, and M. Dahood, Psalms (AB), 1:90. For an Ugaritic example of the heart/liver as the source of joy, see G. R. Driver, Canaanite Myths and Legends, 47-48: “her [Anat’s] liver swelled with laughter, her heart was filled with joy, the liver of Anat with triumph.” “Heart” is used in the translation above for the sake of English idiom; the expression “my liver sings” would seem odd indeed to the modern reader.
verses.commentary:
30:12 "that my soul may sing praise to You"
The "my soul" is literally "glory" (BDB 458). The same
consonants also mean "liver" (BDB 458, KB 456). The UBS Text Project (p. 209)
suggests it could be understood as

- referring to the psalmist himself (i.e., inner most being—liver) by the
term (LXX, NKJV, NRSV, TEV, JPSOA)

- a vocative, "O Glory," referring to YHWH
(UBS Text Project gives this option a "B" rating), making it parallel to "O
Lord, my God" of v. 12b

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means
that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of
us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are
priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the
major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be
thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Does God heal all faithful followers?

- Explain why Ps. 30:5 is such an important verse.

- Is Ps. 30:6 a positive or negative statement?

- How are Ps. 30:9 and 12 related?

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- The introduction, which is in the MT, is not original (i.e., not in DSS
psalms). It was obviously added later. I do not accept these introductions
as inspired (see Gleason Archer, Encyclopedia of Biblical Difficulties,
p. 243), therefore, I do not comment on them.

- For a brief discussion on the superscriptions in the MT, see Introduction
to the Psalms, IV. Authorship.
